_comment: The few panel facts that are NOT in the KiCad output or the firmware tables.
Everything else in bmcv_panel.json is derived - see tools/gen_panel_spec.py.
Each entry here should either be measured off a real module or resolved from
the schematic, and then moved out of 'assumptions'.

panel._note: matches web/bmcv_panel.png; board_offset_mm is derived, the board is centred in the panel.

_note: axis and body_mm are read from the RV13 footprint in BMCV.kicad_pcb.
travel_mm is the wiper stroke, which the CAD data does not carry. Measured
off the slot drawn in web/bmcv_panel.png: the slot spans board x 13.38..66.53
(53.15mm) centred on RV13 at 40.0, leaving ~49mm of handle-centre travel once
the 4mm handle is accounted for.
Panel-space centres of the four M3 slots, in the same coordinates as
panel.width_mm - not board space, since they are outside the board.
Measured off the dark shapes in web/bmcv_panel.png, which is the only
place the panel's own outline exists; the KiCad data here is the PCB.
Only a host that draws its own screws needs them.
AD7367 has two ADCs (A, B), each 2:1 muxed by the ADDR line, so the four
converter slots are A1/B1 (one ADDR phase) and A2/B2 (the other).
dacadc_dma_next() samples the ADDR pin into `offset` BEFORE toggling it,
so which phase lands in adc_i[0..1] vs adc_i[2..3] cannot be settled by
reading the code.
Resolved by the panel: with A2/B2 in adc slots 0/1, input_adc_idx {2,3,0,1}
puts inputs 0..3 on J9,J10,J11,J12 - top-left, top-right, bottom-left,
bottom-right, the same reading order as everything else on the panel.
The other phase would number them 2,3,0,1 across the panel, which nothing
else on the module does.

assumptions: mounting slot centres measured off web/bmcv_panel.png, not derived from CAD
slider travel_mm = 49.0, measured off the slot in the panel artwork rather than the wiper itself
the 80x108mm board is centred in a 81x128.5mm panel; matches web/bmcv_panel.png
